items.q: Does standing near a radioactive source make you radioactive?
items.misconception: Yes, you become radioactive just by being near it.
items.why: Irradiation is exposure to rays; contamination is radioactive material on or in you.

items.correct: Alpha — most ionising but least penetrating (stopped by paper).
items.misconception: Gamma, because it is most penetrating.
items.why: Alpha ionises strongly but is easily absorbed; gamma penetrates far but ionises weakly.

items.q: Can heating a source change its half-life?
items.correct: No — half-life is fixed and unaffected by temperature or pressure.
items.misconception: Yes, heating speeds up decay and shortens half-life.
items.random_wrong: Half-life depends on how much sample you have.
items.why: Radioactive decay is random and independent of physical conditions or amount.
